results.name: cpu_get_type
results.evidence: param_1==0 branch strncmp's the cached vendor id string DAT_006e35ac against "AuthenticAMD"/"GenuineIntel"/"CyrixInstead"/"CentaurHauls" and returns a 1-4 vendor enum; param_1==1 recurses into itself for the vendor, then decodes DAT_00721e64 (cpuid EAX family/model) into a small integer code via nested switches, lazily calling FUN_00540da0 first if DAT_00721e88 is uninitialized.
results.summary: Lazily gathers CPUID data (via FUN_00540da0) then, depending on mode, returns either a CPU-vendor enum or a finer processor-model code derived from vendor + family/model bits, presumably to index a friendly CPU name table.

results.name: cpu_query_identification
results.evidence: Toggles the EFLAGS ID bit to test CPUID support, then calls the already-named cpuid_basic_info/cpuid_Version_info/cpuid_brand_part1_info/cpuid_brand_part2_info/cpuid_brand_part3_info stubs and stores their results into DAT_006e35ac (12-byte vendor id string), DAT_00721e64 (family/model/stepping), and the DAT_00721e78.. cache/brand fields.
results.summary: Detects CPUID availability and, if present, fills the module's cached CPU-identification globals (vendor string, feature/family DWORD, extended cache and brand-string leaves) from the CPUID instruction.

results.name: engine_initialize_subsystems
results.evidence: timeBeginPeriod/QueryPerformanceFrequency, delay-loads d3d9.dll!Direct3DCreate9, dsound.dll!DirectSoundCreate8, dinput8.dll!DirectInput8Create and shfolder.dll!SHGetFolderPathA, then calls data_file_open, math_initialize, FUN_00537f90, FUN_00511da0 and (on success) sound_initialize.
results.summary: Top-level engine bring-up routine: sets timer resolution, resolves the D3D9/DirectSound/DirectInput/Shell entry points, and initializes the data-file, math, and (conditionally) sound subsystems, returning success/failure.

results.name: engine_shutdown_subsystems
results.evidence: Mirror of engine_initialize_subsystems's teardown: calls cache_file_unload, rasterizer_shutdown, periodic_function_tables_free, data_file_close, sound_dispose, frees several GlobalAlloc'd buffers, and calls timeEndPeriod(1).
results.summary: Tears down the engine subsystems started by engine_initialize_subsystems: unloads the cache file, shuts down the rasterizer, disposes sound, and releases assorted global buffers.

results.name: shell_winmain
results.evidence: param_1/param_2/param_3/param_4 are stored positionally into DAT_007461c0/_cc/DAT_006e35c0/_cc exactly like WinMain(hInstance,hPrevInstance,lpCmdLine,nCmdShow); reads registry key "Software\\Microsoft\\Microsoft Games\\Halo" value "FIRSTRUN", loads eula.dll!EBUEula on first run, then parses ~20 "-flag" command-line switches ("-window","-nosound","-safemode",...) via FUN_00542760.
results.prototype: int __stdcall shell_winmain(void *hInstance, void *hPrevInstance, char *lpCmdLine, int nCmdShow)
results.summary: The game's WinMain-equivalent: shows the EULA on first run, parses the command line into engine flags, and drives the rest of process start-up (window class registration, cache reservation, subsystem init) before entering the main loop.

results.name: shell_pump_windows_messages
results.evidence: Classic PeekMessageA/TranslateMessage/DispatchMessageA pump loop, with a special case that instead calls through the Keystone UI dispatch pointer DAT_00721eb0 (Call_KsTranslateAccelerator, resolved in FUN_00542ad0) when the UI system (DAT_00721ea4/DAT_00721e9c) is active.
results.summary: Drains the Win32 message queue each frame, routing messages through the Keystone UI accelerator translator when the UI library is loaded and otherwise through the normal Translate/DispatchMessage path.

results.name: clipboard_get_text
results.evidence: IsClipboardFormatAvailable(CF_TEXT)+OpenClipboard(DAT_007461c4)+GetClipboardData(1)+GlobalLock, then _strncpy(param_1,_Source,param_2) copies the clipboard text into the caller's buffer before CloseClipboard.
results.summary: Copies the current CF_TEXT clipboard contents into the caller-supplied buffer (param_1, capacity param_2), returning 1 on success or 0 if no text is available.

results.name: game_window_proc
results.evidence: Ends with DefWindowProcA(hwnd,message,wparam,lparam); tests wparam against 0x5b/0x5c (VK_LWIN/VK_RWIN) to suppress the Windows key while the game window is active (matches the "-nowinkey"/"-nowindowskey" flags seen in shell_winmain), and tests message==0x100 (WM_KEYDOWN) with wparam 0xd/0x1b (VK_RETURN/VK_ESCAPE) to drive chat_submit_input/chat_close. The prior name 'scenario_trigger_volume_test_point' does not match this Win32 message-handling code at all and is corrected here.
results.summary: The game's main window procedure: intercepts the Windows-key chord to pause/minimize the game, routes Enter/Escape to the chat box, forwards Keystone UI accelerator translation, and defers everything else to DefWindowProcA.

results.name: command_line_parse_to_argv
results.evidence: Walks the command-line string in unaff_EDI splitting on '-'-prefixed tokens and whitespace, converts embedded quote characters to spaces, counts tokens, GlobalAlloc's an argv-style pointer array (*param_1 = count) and fills it with pointers into the (mutated in place) original buffer.
results.summary: Tokenizes the raw Halo command line into a GlobalAlloc'd argv-style array of substring pointers, writing the token count out through param_1.

results.name: command_line_check_flag
results.evidence: Iterates the argv array (DAT_00721e90, count DAT_00721e94) built by command_line_parse_to_argv, __stricmp's each '-'-prefixed entry against param_1, and if found optionally writes the following non-flag argument through the caller's out-pointer (unaff_EDI).
results.summary: Looks up a named '-flag' in the parsed command line and reports whether it is present, optionally returning its following value argument.

results.name: os_platform_identify
results.evidence: GetVersionExA(&local_94) then maps _OSVERSIONINFOA.dwPlatformId: VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS(1)->DAT_00721ef0=2, VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT(2)->DAT_00721ef0=3, anything else->1, caching the result in the module-global platform code.
results.summary: Queries GetVersionExA and caches a small platform-family code (Win9x vs WinNT vs other) into DAT_00721ef0 for later feature gating.

results.name: security_check_write_access
results.evidence: On NT platforms (os_platform_identify result >= 3) it opens the thread/process token, DuplicateToken(SecurityImpersonation), builds a Everyone-group SID, InitializeSecurityDescriptor/InitializeAcl/AddAccessAllowedAce(GENERIC_WRITE), then calls AccessCheck against a GENERIC_MAPPING and caches the boolean result in DAT_0069eab0.
results.summary: Determines (once, then caches) whether the current thread token has write access under a synthetic ACL, used to detect restricted/limited-user accounts on NT systems; always reports access granted on non-NT platforms.

results.name: security_check_cleanup
results.evidence: Frees the LocalAlloc'd SID/ACL buffers and closes the process/impersonation token handles allocated by security_check_write_access, matching that function's local variable layout (unaff_EBX/EDI = the two LocalAlloc pointers, *(unaff_EBP-0x1c) = the SID, *(unaff_EBP-0x24/-0x20) = the token handles).
results.summary: Releases the SID, ACL/security-descriptor buffer, and token handles allocated inside security_check_write_access.

results.name: keystone_library_load
results.evidence: LoadLibraryA("keystone.dll") then GetProcAddress for "KeystoneCreate" and the full set of "Call_Ks*"/"Call_KW_*"/"Call_KC_*" exports, storing each into the DAT_00721ea0..DAT_00721edc function-pointer globals used throughout the shell module's UI code; also normalizes the process locale and caches the current directory as a wide string.
results.summary: Loads the Keystone UI middleware DLL and resolves all of its Call_Ks*/Call_KW*/Call_KC* entry points into globals, unless networking-only mode (DAT_007196f4) disables the UI.

results.name: keystone_library_unload
results.evidence: FreeLibrary(DAT_00721e9c) (the keystone.dll handle set by keystone_library_load) and zeroes every Call_Ks*/Call_KW*/Call_KC* function-pointer global that function populated.
results.summary: Unloads keystone.dll and clears all of its cached UI entry-point function pointers.

results.name: game_single_instance_check
results.evidence: CreateMutexA loop over a "Global\\{cff2f1a0-500e-4fae-a789-...}"-style named mutex table (falling back to a non-"Global\\" name on pre-Win2000 via dwMajorVersion<5); on ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS it finds the existing "Halo"/"Halo" window, restores/foregrounds it, and _exit(1)s the new instance.
results.summary: Enforces a single running instance of Halo by taking a named mutex; if another copy already holds it, brings that window to the foreground and terminates the current process.

results.name: dialog_center_on_screen
results.evidence: Only acts when param_2==0x110 (WM_INITDIALOG); computes the desktop client rect via GetDesktopWindow/GetClientRect and MoveWindow's param_1 to be centered, matching the classic 'center this dialog' WM_INITDIALOG handler idiom.
results.summary: WM_INITDIALOG handler snippet that centers the given dialog/window over the desktop.

results.name: exception_filter_crash_reporter
results.evidence: *param_1 (the exception record pointer) is compared to -0x3fffff03 == 0xC00000FD == STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW to special-case stack switching; loads faultrep.dll!ReportFault, formats "Halo", "MS Sans Serif" and a GlobalAlloc'd DLGTEMPLATE for CreateDialogIndirectParamA, and references "dxdiag.txt", "debug.txt", "network.log" and ".\\Watson\\dw15.exe -x -s %u" for the Dr. Watson crash report pipeline.
results.summary: The game's unhandled-exception filter: builds and shows the 'Halo has crashed' report dialog, collects dxdiag/debug/network logs, and hands off to Dr. Watson (dw15.exe) or faultrep.dll to submit a crash report to watson.microsoft.com.

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_construct
results.evidence: Calls FUN_00627dc1 (base std::exception init) then installs vtable &PTR_FUN_00655080, zero-initializes a second embedded SSO string (offsets 0x20/0x24), and constructs the first embedded string (offset 0x10) from the message argument via FUN_0057b830 - the standard MSVC 'exception subclass with an embedded std::string message' constructor shape, matching the sibling destructor at 0x578310.
results.summary: Constructs a custom std::exception-derived error object (used by the hardware-requirements script parser) that carries two embedded string members, initializing the first from the supplied message string.

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_destruct
results.evidence: Resets the vtable to &PTR_FUN_00655080 (this class's own level, the standard C++ dtor idiom), frees both embedded SSO string buffers when their capacity fields exceed 15, then chains to exception::~exception(in_ECX).
results.summary: Destructor for the base hardware-requirements-parser exception class: frees its two embedded string buffers and calls the std::exception base destructor.

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_scalar_deleting_destructor
results.evidence: Calls hwreq_parse_exception_destruct(FUN_00578310) then conditionally _free(in_ECX) when the low bit of param_1 is set - the canonical MSVC 'scalar deleting destructor' (operator-delete-on-destroy) pattern.
results.summary: Scalar deleting destructor for the base hwreq parser exception class: destructs the object and optionally frees its storage.

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_variant_b_destruct
results.evidence: Installs a distinct vtable (&PTR_FUN_0065508c) then immediately calls hwreq_parse_exception_destruct (FUN_00578310), the standard 'derived destructor resets vtable to its own level then chains to the base destructor' pattern; no strings distinguish what this sibling exception type represents.
results.summary: Destructor for a second exception class sharing the same string-pair layout as hwreq_parse_exception_destruct's class but with a different vtable/RTTI identity (exact distinguishing purpose unclear).

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_variant_b_scalar_deleting_destructor
results.evidence: Calls hwreq_parse_exception_variant_b_destruct (FUN_005783b0) then conditionally _free(in_ECX) based on the low bit of param_1, matching the scalar-deleting-destructor idiom of FUN_00578390.
results.summary: Scalar deleting destructor for the 'variant b' hwreq exception class.

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_variant_c_destruct
results.evidence: Installs vtable &PTR_FUN_00655098 then chains to hwreq_parse_exception_destruct (FUN_00578310), the same derived-destructor pattern as FUN_005783b0 but with a third distinct vtable.
results.summary: Destructor for a third sibling exception class in the same hierarchy as hwreq_parse_exception_destruct, distinguished only by vtable/RTTI.

results.name: hwreq_parse_exception_variant_c_scalar_deleting_destructor
results.evidence: Calls hwreq_parse_exception_variant_c_destruct (FUN_005783e0) then conditionally _free(in_ECX), the scalar-deleting-destructor idiom.
results.summary: Scalar deleting destructor for the 'variant c' hwreq exception class.

results.name: hwreq_device_override_list_upsert
results.evidence: Walks a node array (stride 0x38, begin/end at param_1+4/+8) comparing each node's embedded SSO key string (offset 4, capacity check at 0x18) to param_2 via __stricmp; on reaching the end without a match it builds a string pair from param_2/param_3 (via hwreq_string_pair_construct/FUN_0057b670) and appends it (FUN_0057b5e0), matching pattern of an associative 'find or insert' used by the requirements parser's device-override table.
results.summary: Looks up param_2 in a linear key/value list of device-override strings and, if absent, inserts a new (param_2,param_3) entry; if present, only rewrites the value's storage without changing the key.

results.name: hwreq_string_pair_destruct
results.evidence: Frees the two embedded SSO string buffers at offsets (0x20/0x34) and (4/0x18) when their capacity fields exceed 15, matching the pair<string,string> node layout used by hwreq_device_override_list_upsert's node array.
results.summary: Destructs a heap-embedded pair of strings, releasing any out-of-line buffers each string owns.

results.name: hwreq_device_override_list_find
results.evidence: Same node array/stride-0x38 walk as hwreq_device_override_list_upsert, __stricmp's each node's key string against unaff_EBX, and on a match strncpy's the node's value string (offset 0x20, SSO capacity check at 0x34) into the caller's buffer, returning 1/0 for found/not-found.
results.summary: Looks up a key in the device-override list and, if found, copies its associated value string into the caller-supplied buffer.

results.name: hwreq_parser_scalar_deleting_destructor
results.evidence: If in_ECX is non-null, calls FUN_0057a010 (the full parser-object destructor, see below) then _free(in_ECX) unconditionally - the scalar-deleting-destructor idiom applied to the main requirements-parser class.
results.summary: Scalar deleting destructor for the hardware-requirements parser object: destructs it via FUN_0057a010 and frees its storage.

results.name: hwreq_symbol_table_find
results.evidence: Constructs a temporary string from param_1 (via FUN_0057bc90), calls FUN_0057b7a0 to search an associative structure, compares the result to a per-object end/sentinel field at offset 0x6a4, and returns 0 (not found) or the value field at offset 0x28 of the matching node.
results.summary: Looks up param_1 as a key in one of the parser object's symbol maps, returning the associated value field or 0 if not present.

results.name: hwreq_token_skip_line
results.evidence: Advances the cursor field at (in_EAX+8) until it consumes a '\r' (and an immediately following '\n'), stores the new position into the 'line start' field (+0x10), and increments the line counter (+0x14).
results.summary: Tokenizer helper that advances the parser's cursor to the start of the next line, updating the cached line-start pointer and line-number counter.

results.name: hwreq_token_skip_whitespace
results.evidence: Advances the cursor field at (in_EDX+8) past ' ' and '\t' characters.
results.summary: Tokenizer helper that skips spaces and tabs at the parser's current cursor position.

results.name: hwreq_parser_report_error
results.evidence: Latches only the first error per line (guarded by a flag at offset 0x20), captures up to 36 characters of the current line for context, and formats "%s on line %d - '%s'" using param_1, the line counter (offset 0x14), and that snippet, storing the result via FUN_0057bc90.
results.summary: Records a parser error message together with the current line number and a snippet of the offending line, for later reporting; ignored if an error was already latched on this line.

results.name: hwreq_token_parse_hex_digit
results.evidence: Classifies the current character as '0'-'9', 'a'-'f', or 'A'-'F', converts it to its 0-15 numeric value and advances the cursor, returning -1 for any other character.
results.summary: Parses a single hexadecimal digit at the cursor, advancing past it and returning its value, or -1 if the character is not a hex digit.

results.name: hwreq_token_parse_number
results.evidence: Skips whitespace, then if the token starts with "0x" parses hex digits via hwreq_token_parse_hex_digit (erroring "Number too large" past 8 digits), otherwise parses decimal digits directly; falls back to hwreq_parser_report_error("Number expected") if neither form matches.
results.summary: Parses a decimal or 0x-prefixed hexadecimal integer literal token, reporting a parser error if no valid number is present.

results.name: hwreq_token_parse_quoted_string
results.evidence: Requires a leading '"' (else hwreq_parser_report_error("Expecting ")), copies characters into the static buffer DAT_00722d58 until the closing '"', erroring "String too long" if the buffer (bounded by DAT_00722e57) overflows.
results.summary: Parses a double-quoted string literal token into a shared static buffer, reporting parser errors for a missing quote or an overlong string.

results.name: hwreq_parser_parse_flag_assignment
results.evidence: Reads a lowercase 'flag' identifier up to '=' or end-of-line (erroring "Flag too long"), then a value that may be a quoted string (erroring "Missing Quote") or a bare token, inserts the pair into the device-override list via hwreq_device_override_list_upsert (FUN_00578410), and special-cases the flag name "OverallGraphicDetail" by additionally recording its value via FUN_0057b6e0.
results.summary: Parses one 'flag = value' assignment line from the requirements script, storing it in the flag table and, for the special OverallGraphicDetail flag, also recording its value for the caller.

results.name: hwreq_token_parse_hex_id
results.evidence: Manually decodes the first hex character and then calls hwreq_token_parse_hex_digit three more times, combining four hex digits (<<0xc,<<8,<<4,identity) into a single 16-bit value, matching the size of a PCI vendor/device ID.
results.summary: Parses a 4-hex-digit token (e.g. a vendor or device ID) into a 16-bit value, returning -1 on any invalid digit.

results.name: hwreq_token_parse_hex_id_byteswap
results.evidence: Calls hwreq_token_parse_hex_id (FUN_00578ef0) then byte-swaps the low 16 bits ((v&0xff)*0x100 + (v>>8&0xff)); used alongside similar 16-bit groups in gamespy_get_client_key_hash's GUID assembly (four groups combined as iVarN*0x10000+iVarM), consistent with parsing the mixed-endian hex groups of a Windows GUID string.
results.summary: Parses a 4-hex-digit token and returns it byte-swapped, used when assembling multi-byte fields (such as a driver GUID) from their textual hex representation.

results.name: hwreq_token_match_keyword
results.evidence: __strnicmp's the cursor against the caller-supplied keyword string in_EDX for its length, then additionally requires the following character to be a delimiter ('>','<','!','=',' ','\r','\t') before reporting a match - the generic keyword-matcher reused (inlined) by the vendor/audiovendor/Requirements/applytoall/propertyset scanners elsewhere in this cluster.
results.summary: Tests whether the parser's cursor is currently positioned at the given keyword, followed by a valid delimiter character, without consuming the token.

results.name: hwreq_d3dcaps_field_resolve
results.evidence: Chains dozens of hwreq_token_match_keyword (FUN_00578fa0) calls against a literal list of IDirect3DDevice9 D3DCAPS9 field names ("Caps2","Caps3","DevCaps","RasterCaps","TextureCaps","MaxTextureBlendStages","VertexShaderVersion", etc.) plus "cpuspeed", using a side table (PTR_DAT_0065e9e0/DAT_0065ea5c/DAT_0065ea10/DAT_0065ea18) to resolve the matched name.
results.summary: Matches the current token against the set of recognized D3DCAPS9 (and cpuspeed) field names used by the hardware-requirements script, resolving it to an internal field descriptor for a subsequent comparison.

results.name: hwreq_parser_evaluate_condition
results.evidence: Parses a comparison operator (==,!=,<,>,<=,>=,&), then for the GUID-comparison branch (unaff_EBX==1) parses four 16-bit hex groups via hwreq_token_parse_hex_id/hwreq_token_parse_hex_id_byteswap to assemble a driver GUID, elsewhere referencing OS-name literals "win95".. "winxp"/"Unknown OS" and error strings "Invalid GUID"/"Invalid driver number"/"Only == or != allowed". The prior name 'gamespy_get_client_key_hash' is unrelated to this code (no GameSpy strings or hashing) and is corrected here.
results.summary: Parses one comparison-operator term of a requirements-script condition (against a driver GUID, driver version number, or OS name) and evaluates it, reporting a parser error for malformed operators or operands.

results.name: hwreq_parser_construct
results.evidence: Sets the parser object's vtable to &PTR_LAB_006721e8, zero-initializes five embedded SSO strings (capacity fields set to 0xf), and builds two circular sentinel nodes via FUN_0057cbf0 (self-referential left/right/parent, isnil flag at +0x2d) stored at offsets 0x1a9 and 0x1ac - the standard MSVC red-black-tree map default-construction pattern, for two separate maps.
results.summary: Constructs the hardware-requirements parser object, default-initializing its embedded strings and the two associative maps (e.g. flag table and device-override table) it maintains.

results.name: hwreq_map_destruct
results.evidence: Calls FUN_0057c310 (a tree-node-destroy helper) over the node array at (in_EAX+4)..(in_EAX+4 root), then frees the array and zeroes the begin/end pointers.
results.summary: Destructs one of the parser's node-array maps, freeing its storage.

results.name: hwreq_parser_destruct
results.evidence: Frees the two large string buffers at param_1[6]/param_1[7] (via FUN_0057b990 cleanup + _free), walks the map at param_1[0x1a9] destroying each contained device-override node via hwreq_string_pair_destruct (FUN_005785b0) - confirming that map's value type is a string pair - then destroys both trees (FUN_0057c310) and frees the five embedded SSO strings if heap-allocated.
results.summary: Full destructor for the hardware-requirements parser object: frees its large scratch buffers, destroys both maps (including each device-override entry's string pair), and releases its embedded strings.

results.name: hwreq_parser_scan_for_vendor_block
results.evidence: Line-by-line scan (using the same skip-to-'\r'/'\n' idiom as hwreq_token_skip_line) checking each line for the "applytoall" or "vendor" keyword (delimiter-checked inline rather than via hwreq_token_match_keyword) and, on a match, dispatching into hwreq_parser_parse_block (FUN_0057af10).
results.summary: Scans forward line by line through the requirements script looking for an 'applytoall' or 'vendor' directive, parsing the matching block when found.

results.name: hwreq_parser_scan_for_applytoall_block
results.evidence: Same line-scanning structure as hwreq_parser_scan_for_vendor_block but checks only for the "applytoall" keyword before dispatching into hwreq_parser_parse_block (FUN_0057af10).
results.summary: Scans forward line by line through the requirements script looking for an 'applytoall' directive, parsing the matching block when found.

results.name: hwreq_parser_parse_propertyset_directive
results.evidence: Scans for "propertyset"/"vendor"/"applytoall" keywords; on "propertyset" requires '=' then a quoted string (hwreq_token_parse_quoted_string), allocates a 0x14-byte node (operator_new) recording the parent parser pointer at offset 0x10, parses the following block via hwreq_parser_parse_block (FUN_0057af10), and on success stores the node into a list via FUN_0057b6e0(in_ECX+0x6a0); reports "Missing =" if '=' is absent.
results.summary: Parses a 'propertyset = "name"' directive from the requirements script, allocating a property-set record, parsing its nested block, and registering it in the parser's property-set list.

results.name: hwreq_parser_parse_vendor_block
results.evidence: Loops scanning for the "vendor" keyword; after '=' either accepts the literal "unknown" or parses a numeric vendor id (hwreq_token_parse_number) and compares it against the detected vendor field at (in_EAX+0x4e4), and on a match parses a following quoted device-name string, erroring "xxx = Device Name expected" otherwise.
results.summary: Parses a 'vendor[=id] { device = "..." ... }'-style block from the requirements script, applying the enclosed directives only when the id matches the detected graphics vendor.

results.name: hwreq_parser_parse_audiovendor_block
results.evidence: Structurally identical to hwreq_parser_parse_vendor_block but scans for the "audiovendor" keyword and compares against the detected audio-vendor field at (in_EAX+0x690) instead of the graphics-vendor field.
results.summary: Parses an 'audiovendor[=id] { device = "..." ... }'-style block from the requirements script, applying the enclosed directives only when the id matches the detected audio-device vendor.

results.name: hwreq_parser_find_requirements_section
results.evidence: Scans lines for the "Requirements" keyword (delimiter-checked) and, once found (or upon reaching end of the buffer), calls hwreq_parser_parse_block (FUN_0057af10) on the field at (unaff_ESI+0x1c).
results.summary: Locates the top-level 'Requirements' section in the hardware compatibility script and begins parsing it.

results.name: hwreq_parser_parse_block
results.evidence: Recursive-descent block parser handling the "vendor"/"audiovendor"/"Requirements" keywords, the literal "unknown", bare condition expressions (via hwreq_token_match_keyword/hwreq_token_parse_number), flag assignments (hwreq_parser_parse_flag_assignment / FUN_00578cf0), and "MaxOverallGraphicDetail"/"OverallGraphicDetail" special-cases, plus if/endif/break-style nesting evidenced by the strings "IF's nested too deep", "Bad IF/ENDIF", "Unexpected ENDIF", "break", "endif".
results.summary: The core parser routine for one nested block of the hardware-requirements script: evaluates conditions, processes flag assignments and graphic-detail directives, and handles if/endif/break control flow, reporting syntax errors as it goes.

results.name: hwreq_parser_create
results.evidence: operator_new(0x6b8) allocates storage sized to the parser object, then hwreq_parser_construct (FUN_00579ef0) is called on it; returns null if the allocation fails.
results.summary: Allocates and default-constructs a new hardware-requirements parser object.

results.name: hwreq_string_assign_cstr
results.evidence: Computes strlen(in_EDX) then forwards to FUN_0057bc90(in_EDX, len) - the shared string construct/assign helper used throughout this cluster - on the implicit 'this' in in_EAX.
results.summary: Assigns a raw null-terminated C string into a managed string object.

results.name: hwreq_device_list_size
results.evidence: Returns 0 if the list's begin pointer (in_ECX+4) is null, otherwise (end - begin)/0x38, matching the 0x38-byte node stride used by hwreq_device_override_list_upsert.
results.summary: Returns the element count of the device-override node list.

results.name: hwreq_device_list_push_back
results.evidence: If the list still has spare capacity (comparing (end-begin)/0x38 against ((capacity-begin)/0x38), the value at param_1 is copy-constructed in place at the current end (FUN_0057ce80) and the end pointer advances by 0x38; otherwise it falls back to the grow-and-insert path FUN_0057b920.
results.summary: Appends one element to the end of the device-override node list, growing the underlying storage first if it is already full.

results.name: hwreq_string_pair_construct
results.evidence: Zero-initializes two embedded SSO strings (capacity fields at param_1+0x18 and +0x34 set to 0xf) and then assigns each from param_2 and param_3 via FUN_0057b830, matching the pair<string,string> layout freed by hwreq_string_pair_destruct.
results.summary: Constructs a heap-embedded pair of two strings from the given source strings, for insertion into the device-override list.

results.name: hwreq_string_destruct
results.evidence: Frees the string's out-of-line buffer (offset 4) when its capacity field (offset 0x18) exceeds the 15-byte SSO threshold, then resets length/capacity/inline-buffer fields to empty.
results.summary: Destructs a single embedded SSO string, releasing its heap buffer if it was not using small-string storage.

results.name: hwreq_map_find_or_insert
results.evidence: Compares the candidate node param_1 against the map's root/rightmost node, uses hwreq_map_key_less_than (FUN_0057bbd0) for ordering and FUN_0057c1a0/FUN_0057c390/FUN_0057cd40/FUN_0057ce10/FUN_0057c5e0 (rotation/insert/iterator helpers) - the shape of an MSVC red-black-tree map's internal lookup/insert dispatch.
results.summary: Internal red-black-tree helper for one of the parser's maps that locates param_1's position (or inserts it) relative to the tree root, returning an iterator-like result through unaff_ESI.

results.name: hwreq_map_key_less_than
results.evidence: Compares the node's embedded key string (offset 4, SSO capacity check at 0x18) against the search key referenced from (in_EAX+0x14) via FUN_0057ce10 (a string-compare helper) and returns whether the comparison result is negative.
results.summary: Red-black-tree key-ordering predicate: returns true if the given node's key string sorts before the map's current search key.
